front.title: User-Mediated Credential Delivery as a Complementary Authorization Primitive for AI Agents

abstract.t:
This document proposes user-mediated credential delivery as a complementary authorization primitive for AI agent frameworks. Rather than delivering credentials through automated channels controlled by the agent or its platform, user-mediated delivery places the authorization decision and credential delivery in the user's trusted context, separate from the agent's execution environment.
This document describes four methods: user-mediated credential delivery, self-describing connection credentials, caller-identity consent differentiation, and discovery-by-introspection. These methods address the human-in-the-loop gap identified in Section 10.7 of [KLRC] and strengthen the authorization foundation that the IETF AI Agent Authentication and Authorization framework depends on. This revision relates the primitive to the gap analysis in [CHEN-UC] and to the intent credential proposed in [INTENT], states how it composes with grant-layer mechanisms, and reports implementation status.
The methods described in this document are patent pending.
